tpm_lessons: Parallel N>=2 within a workflow burst-triggers the Anthropic TPM cap (~1M tokens/min sustained on our subscription).
6 workflows in parallel, each running sequentially internally, also hit cap on first attempt — only q1 and q2 survived cleanly.
Sequential retry per workflow (1 at a time, 2-3 at a time after cool-down) was the only reliable path. Each workflow ~1.4M tokens / ~5 min.
Total tokens burned across all v2 attempts: ~30M+. Wall time: ~90 min including retries.

comparison_to_published.caveat: DO NOT publish this comparison. Our setup differs: (a) we sampled SMALLEST haystack per type (script-cap workaround), not random; (b) N=3 per question, not the full 500; (c) Opus 4.7 vs whatever model others used; (d) our raw 19% is far below published 60% Full-Context — suggests Opus's long-context retrieval is more conservative (refuses more) than the published baseline's model.

real_takeaways: Pooled across 6 questions × N=3 (21 total runs per condition), compact wins +38pp absolute (57% vs 19%). Large effect.
Compact wins in 3 of 6 questions, ties 2, loses 1. The 1 loss (snapper) is informative: compress agent biased to user-stated facts, lost an assistant recommendation needle.
Two ties bracket the curve: q0 (both fail at floor, needle pruned) and q4 (both succeed at ceiling, fact obvious).

The 4 compact wins (combining clean wins + dominance) all share a pattern: RAW refuses ('context does not contain answer') while COMPACT gives a real answer. Compression doesn't add information — it just restructures so the answering AI can find what's already there.
Raw 19% is a low number, but it reflects Opus 4.7's conservative refusal habit on long-context Q&A more than a real memory ceiling. Raw refuses 14/17 times = 82% refusal rate.
Compact stddev > 0 on q1, q2, q5 — same digest can give different answers run-to-run. Need N>3 for stable stddev estimate.
memory_inc_positioning_implications: memory.inc claims 94.8% by SOLVING the long-context refusal problem at the retrieval layer. Our compact at 57% on cherry-picked easy samples is far from that.
But our 'raw' baseline (19%) is also far below their 60% Full-Context number — comparison apples-to-oranges. We need same baseline before any claim.
Real next step for category entry: run the full LongMemEval-S 500 with consistent setup. Our cherry-pick + N=3 is not in the same league as their published numbers.
honest_recommendation: Do not publish any percentage from this pilot. It is methodologically too caveated.

What CAN be claimed internally: compact mode preserves answer-finding ability on long-context questions where the bare model refuses to engage. We have a directional signal that our /raw/hub/<slug>?digest=1&compact=1 endpoint is doing useful work.
Next investment: solve TPM throttling by using async pacing + retries in the harness, then run full 500 questions. Estimated 50M+ tokens, ~10 hours on subscription. Sane to do once.

Independently solve memory contamination: drop subagents entirely for the answer/compress role and use `claude -p` with --no-resume + explicit no-memory flag, OR build a custom 'evaluation' agent type that doesn't load MEMORY.md.
